items.question: What does a B2B SaaS copywriter and technical writer do?
items.answer: I turn a technical product into content your audience understands and wants to use: SEO articles, tutorials with real code, comparisons, landing page copy, and videos. Unlike a generalist copywriter, I test the product, write the code, and explain why a developer should choose it.

items.question: Do you write copy for landing and product pages?
items.answer: Yes. Alongside technical content, I do B2B SaaS copywriting for landing pages, product pages, and integration pages, with the same approach: concrete benefits, real examples, and no marketing fluff.

items.question: Do you offer YouTube content creation?
items.answer: Yes. My channel has 12,500+ subscribers and 350+ published videos. I create product demos, integration videos, reviews, and Python tutorials that show your tool actually working.

items.question: What about LinkedIn content creation?
items.answer: Yes. I adapt each technical piece into LinkedIn posts and also distribute it on Medium, Dev.to, and GitHub, so your content reaches the B2B audience where it already is instead of depending only on your blog.

items.question: What kind of companies do you work with?
items.answer: B2B SaaS companies, APIs, AI platforms, fintech, and developer tools. I've worked with companies like EODHD APIs, ZenRows, ScrapingBee, Snowball Analytics, Financial Modeling Prep, and Unstract.

items.question: How do you measure results?
items.answer: With data, not impressions. Every link in my articles, videos, and posts carries UTM tags, so your Google Analytics shows exactly how many visits, sign-ups, and conversions come from each piece of content and each channel: Google, YouTube, LinkedIn, or Medium. On top of that, I track organic traffic and Google rankings.

items.question: Which languages do you write in?
items.answer: English and Spanish. I can create content natively in both languages or adapt existing pieces for another market.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with you?
items.answer: It depends on the scope. The Starter, Growth, and Authority packages are a starting point, and the final proposal is tailored to your case. Send me your project and I'll get back to you with a proposal.

steps.title: Diagnosis
steps.pain: "We get traffic, but nobody signs up"

faq.question: How is a B2B SaaS copywriter different from a generalist?
faq.answer: A B2B SaaS copywriter understands long sales cycles, multiple decision-makers, and technical products. On top of that, I'm a developer: I test the product and write with real examples, which is what convinces a technical audience.

faq.question: Do you need access to our product?
faq.answer: Whenever possible, yes. A trial account or a demo lets me write about what your product really does and spot the arguments that matter most to your users.

faq.question: Do you write in English and Spanish?
faq.answer: Yes, in both languages, so you can launch the same page in several markets without a literal translation.

faq.question: How do you measure whether the copy works?
faq.answer: With each page's conversion rate and UTM tags on the links that send it traffic. That way you know which page and which channel bring the most sign-ups.

faq.question: Can it be combined with SEO content or video?
faq.answer: Yes, and that's what works best: the article or video attracts the reader and the landing page converts them. It's part of the Growth and Authority packages.

faq.question: Do you have your own audience on LinkedIn?
faq.answer: Yes. I publish technical content on LinkedIn and run a newsletter with 1,600+ subscribers. The same techniques I use there are the ones I apply to your company's content.

faq.question: How does LinkedIn ghostwriting work?
faq.answer: We start with a call to capture your voice, opinions, and stories. I draft the posts, you review and approve them, and they go out under your name. I write for founders, CTOs, and the company page.

faq.question: Where does the content for the posts come from?
faq.answer: From your product and content that already exists: articles, videos, docs, and customer stories. That way each post teaches something concrete and leads to a longer piece.

faq.question: How often do you post?
faq.answer: We set it in the editorial calendar based on your goals. Consistency matters more than posting every day.

faq.question: How do you measure results on LinkedIn?
faq.answer: With each post's reach and engagement and, above all, UTM tags on the links, to see how many visits, sign-ups, and demos come from LinkedIn.

faq.question: Can it be combined with YouTube and SEO?
faq.answer: Yes, and it's what I recommend: one article or video becomes several posts, and each channel reinforces the others.
